task.description: Design the fix for GH #576 / ISS-0622, per ISSUE-FIXER's verified diagnosis and recommended strategy (Step 1, handoff dbe09af3). CONFIRMED root cause: src/api/middleware/quota_enforcement.zig's readUsageForDimension -> countRows / maxColumn / countRowsWhereRecent each call pool.acquire() and issue UNQUALIFIED SQL against instance_projections, instance_waits, and dead_letter_items -- three tables that exist ONLY in tenant_default (and per-tenant SCHEMA-mode schemas), never in public. Under .LEGACY_RLS storage mode (the default for any tenant never promoted to SCHEMA mode), pool.zig's applyRequestStorageRouting sets search_path=public only, so these reads are structurally unreachable -- confirmed live (to_regclass on all three public.* variants returns NULL) and empirically (TC-EXP-601-02/04 fail exactly here). APPROVED STRATEGY: explicit schema-qualification, mirroring how src/db/pool.zig's applyRequestStorageRouting itself resolves storage_mode and computes a schema name before issuing SQL. Use the SAME exported helpers pool.zig already provides: schemaNameForTenant() (pool.zig:137) for the SCHEMA-mode schema name, and tenant_context.getStorageMode()/hasStorageMode()/resolveAndCacheStorageMode() to determine which mode applies. Design exactly how readUsageForDimension/countRows/etc should resolve and inject the correct schema prefix (tenant_default for LEGACY_RLS, tenant_{slug} for SCHEMA mode) into each of the currently-unqualified queries against instance_projections, instance_waits, dead_letter_items -- WITHOUT touching repository_artifacts (already correctly public-qualified, untouched by GH-566/ISS-0617) or any other table these functions reference. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE (documented, do not revisit): creating public-schema views/copies of these three tables -- this would reproduce the dual-schema-shadow anti-pattern GBL-134/135/136 exist to dismantle (see docs/anti-patterns.md, ISS-0185/GH-518 entry). SIBLING FINDING (note only, do NOT fix in this design): src/admin/tenant_lifecycle.zig::resetTestTenant() (lines 100-128) has the identical unqualified-read-via-pool pattern against instance_projections. Assess whether it's genuinely the same latent defect (if trivial to note, mention in the design's out-of-scope section for a future issue) -- do not fix it here, this issue's scope is quota_enforcement.zig only. Also assess (for your own understanding, note findings but do not act unless directly blocking): src/scheduler/scheduler.zig's appendEventInTx receives a *db.Conn parameter rather than self-acquiring from pool, so its search_path is set by whatever caller passes the connection in -- structurally different from quota_enforcement.zig's self-acquire-per-call pattern, likely NOT the same bug class, but worth one sentence of due diligence in the design doc so a future reader doesn't have to re-derive this.
acceptance_criteria: Design specifies exactly how each of the 3 affected queries (instance_projections, instance_waits, dead_letter_items reads) gets schema-qualified per resolved storage_mode
Design reuses pool.zigs existing schemaNameForTenant/tenant_context helpers rather than inventing new ones
Design confirms repository_artifacts / file_count / file_bytes dimension reads are untouched (already correct)
Design confirms TC-EXP-601-02 and TC-EXP-601-04 (the quota-guard assertions, not the separate instance_waits fixture-insert issue already tracked elsewhere) will pass after the fix
Sibling tenant_lifecycle.zig finding noted in an out-of-scope section, not fixed
No implementation code present in the design artefact

result.summary: Designed schema-qualification fix for ISS-0622/GH-576: readUsageForDimension resolves the tenant's storage_mode schema once per call (via a new private resolveTenantSchema helper reusing pool.zig's resolveAndCacheStorageMode / schemaNameForTenant and tenant_context's hasStorageMode/getStorageMode caching), then passes an already-schema-qualified table identifier (built via std.fmt.bufPrint into a stack buffer, no allocator) down to countRows/countRowsWhereRecent/maxColumn instead of each helper re-deriving it. .LEGACY_RLS resolves to the literal 'tenant_default' (confirmed via configureTestSearchPath's own convention and schemaNameForTenant's default-UUID branch); .SCHEMA resolves via the existing schemaNameForTenant. Confirmed SQL-injection safety: the interpolated segment is always either the 'tenant_default' constant or a hyphen-stripped, already-authenticated UUID via schemaNameForTenant, which performs no identifier quoting itself but relies on the UUID character set containing no SQL metacharacters (same trust boundary pool.zig already relies on for the identical interpolation it performs today). repository_artifacts (.file_count/.file_bytes) branches are explicitly untouched and confirmed already-correct. Flagged tableStorageBytes (.entity_storage, pg_total_relation_size(...::regclass)) as a fifth call site with the identical bug not named in the task's helper list -- recommended BACKEND-DEV fix it in the same pass. Confirmed via full read of tests/integration/exp601_tier_quota_test.zig that TC-EXP-601-02 and TC-EXP-601-04's quota-guard (429) assertions will pass after this fix, independent of TC-EXP-601-04's separately-tracked instance_waits fixture-INSERT issue. Sibling tenant_lifecycle.zig::resetTestTenant() finding noted in Out of scope (same bug pattern, different call site, not fixed here); scheduler.zig::appendEventInTx due-diligence note included (structurally different, receives *db.Conn from caller rather than self-acquiring, likely not the same bug class). No implementation code present in the design artefact. python tools/lint_design_artefact.py exits 0 (BLOCKER=0, MAJOR=0, MINOR=6 -- all MINOR findings are expected/benign, consistent with the sibling ISS-0617 design doc's own public.tenant/public.tenant_schemas references and the pre-existing ISS-NNNN 4-digit vs linter's \d{1,3} regex mismatch).
